CONTRACT (distribution-contract.ts):
- Closed component kinds CONTROL_ROOM/DAEMON/IDE_ADAPTER/MCP_BRIDGE/PROVIDER_ADAPTER, frozen; 2 refusal layers; 34 stable refusal reasons, frozen.
- `DistributionManifest` deliberately has NO signature field. The signature sits beside the manifest on the container, so "excluded from the bytes it signs" is a STRUCTURAL property rather than a field the codec must remember to skip — there is no skip list to get wrong.
- `canonicalJson` sorts keys by UTF-16 code unit and emits no whitespace; both byte functions run through it, so one tree yields one byte string on every host.
- `normalizeLogicalPath` strips exactly one leading `./` and refuses everything else that could canonicalize differently across hosts: backslash, colon (drive/ADS), leading `/`, empty/dot/dot-dot segments, and segments ending in a dot or space. NFC + `isWellFormed()` are required, so a decomposed path is a refusal rather than a second spelling of the same file.
- Dependency-free as required: it imports only `isNonEmptyString` and the `GitObjectFormat` type from inside @moe/contracts. No clock, no filesystem, no environment read, no crypto, no authority or lifecycle semantics.

PARSER (distribution-parser.ts):
- `refusedBy` is the caller's layer everywhere, never a literal — the same malformed bytes are a packager fault at build time and a startup fault at admission, and a hardcoded layer would lie about one of them. The suite pins this by refusing the same input through both layers.
- Source provenance picks the digest width FROM the declared object format (sha1 -> 40, sha256 -> 64) instead of inferring the format from the length, so a 40-hex value declared `sha256` is a refusal rather than a silently accepted sha1.
- Assets are sorted by path and deduplicated case-INSENSITIVELY, because a Windows checkout cannot carry both `src/A.ts` and `src/a.ts`; accepting both would produce a manifest no host can materialize.
- `parseIdentities` is one routine over both identity lists, parameterised by `idKey`, so skills and templates cannot drift apart in their duplicate/ordering rules. Only skills get the strict `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$` pattern — template IDs are real paths like `.codex/agent-instructions.md`.
- Container admission requires the carried asset key set to EQUAL the manifest's declared paths in both directions: extra bytes nobody signed for are as wrong as a missing asset.
- Reused rather than reimplemented: `decodeBoundedJsonBytes` for the bounded decode, and `hasExactKeys`/`isHex64`/`isPlainRecord`/`isSafeArray`/`isSafeCount` from runtime-guards. `isPlainRecord` is what makes the hostile-input cases refuse — it rejects proxies (checked before `Array.isArray`, which throws on a revoked proxy), exotic prototypes, symbol keys and accessors.

BRIDGES: both modules have their one-line LF `.js` bridge naming their own sibling (`export * from "./distribution-contract.ts";` / `"./distribution-parser.ts";`), verified byte-wise with `od -c`.

DESIGN, and the properties an optimistic implementation gets wrong:
- Trust is never self-derived. Every comparison is manifest-versus-EXPECTATION; nothing is compared component-to-component. That is what makes the "entirely stale but mutually consistent" case refuse: two components agreeing on the same wrong sourceSha agree perfectly, and agreement is not evidence. The doc comment on StartupDistributionExpectation states the rule so a later editor cannot reintroduce a cross-component consensus check by accident.
- Ordering is load-bearing and pinned by the suite. Expectation validity, then component-SET shape, then per-component checks. Inside the set check, DUPLICATE is tested before the missing/extra comparison — otherwise `[daemon, control-room, daemon]` has the correct ID *set* and a set-equality check would admit a doubled component.
- SIGNING_KEY_UNTRUSTED is decided BEFORE the signature port is invoked, so an untrusted key never reaches crypto. The suite proves it with a spy that must record zero calls, not merely by the returned reason.
- A throwing port is caught and mapped to SIGNATURE_PORT_FAILED rather than propagating: a crypto backend that dies must fail closed, not crash the caller into an ambiguous state.
- The admitted result carries `componentIds` and `sourceSha` only. No function-valued property, no launch capability, deeply frozen — the suite asserts the absence of function values rather than trusting the shape.
- Signature verification is an injected port, so the kernel stays pure: no crypto choice, no key material, no environment read, no clock.
- Existing authorities are composed, not restated: the api pins and schema hash are COMPARED against caller-supplied values, so `createCompatGate` remains the control room's authority and the daemon keeps its own COMPATIBILITY refusal. This gate supplies the expected values those layers deliberately do not hold.
- `isUsableExpectation` is documented as a fail-closed sanity gate rather than a hostile-input parser — the expectation is the host's own configuration. It still refuses an empty trusted-key list and an empty component map, because either makes every downstream comparison vacuously satisfiable.

DETERMINISM, and the three places it could have leaked:
- `aggregateDigestHex` hashes the SORTED (path, digest) pairs with explicit LF framing after each field. Framing matters and is not decoration: unframed concatenation lets `a/b` + digest and `a` + `/b`+digest collide, so two different asset sets could share an aggregate.
- Asset paths go through `normalizeLogicalPath` before hashing, so a `./`-prefixed spelling and a bare spelling produce one path and one digest.
- No clock, no filesystem read, no environment access, no child process, no absolute path anywhere in the module. Nothing host-specific can reach the bytes.

SKILL AND KEY DISCIPLINE:
- Identities come from the production `validateSkillManifestBytes`; the digest embedded is that validator's own `identityDigest`, not a second hash computed here. Malformed bytes refuse SKILL_IDENTITY_INVALID at the packager rather than being embedded.
- Same-ID substitution is refused by `parseDistributionManifest`, which sees both entries and returns SKILL_IDENTITY_DUPLICATE at the DISTRIBUTION_PACKAGER layer. Deliberately NOT deduplicated here — merging two skills that claim one ID is precisely the silent substitution the 2026-08-07 roadmap amendment forbids.
- Build input is exact-key, so an undeclared `runtimeSkills` payload refuses BUILD_INPUT_INVALID instead of being embedded or dropped. Runtime/user/project skills stay external provenance.
- The private key is a parameter used once for `sign` and is never logged, returned, embedded or persisted. `publicKeyHex` exports only the raw 32-byte public tail of the SPKI DER.

THE ORDERING PROPERTY THAT MATTERS: nothing launches until the WHOLE set is admitted. Decode all, recompute all, verify the set, and only then loop the launch port. A per-component launch loop would start a valid daemon beside a tampered control room — the split state a distribution gate exists to prevent. Every one of the 13 tamper cases asserts the launch port recorded ZERO calls, not merely that the result was a refusal.

REFUSALS ARE PROPAGATED, NOT RE-MINTED. A decode failure returns the parser's own refusal object and an admission failure returns the verifier's, both unchanged, so `refusedBy` stays truthful about which layer decided. Only three reasons originate here, and each is genuinely a startup-tool fact: EXPECTATION_INVALID (malformed input shape), SIGNING_KEY_UNTRUSTED (the key map is the tool's, not the kernel's), LAUNCH_PORT_FAILED.

SIGNING_KEY_UNTRUSTED is decided before any crypto call — a container whose signingKeyId has no entry in `trustedPublicKeys` refuses at decode time. Without that pre-check the missing key would surface as a port failure and report SIGNATURE_INVALID, which is a materially different and misleading fact: "we do not trust this signer" is not "this signature is forged".

`aggregateDigestHex` here MIRRORS the packager's framing exactly (sorted pairs, LF after each field). Any drift between the two would reject every honest build, so the comment says so at both ends; the byte-rebuild tests are what hold them together.

Ed25519 verification rebuilds the public key from the raw 32-byte hex by prefixing the SPKI DER header `302a300506032b6570032100`, measured working on Node v24.16.0 in step 1. The trusted map therefore holds raw hex, not PEM.

LIVE PINS — the step's "supplied live pins rather than literals" requirement, which the suite did NOT satisfy until now. The integration test previously used hand-written pin literals (`"1.4.0"` etc.) and a fabricated `"9".repeat(64)` schema hash. Those made every test pass while packaging a distribution the control room would refuse to run. Fixed:
- `PINS` and `SCHEMA_HASH` now read from `GENERATED_CONTRACT_PINS` (live `contractDigest` 1d96f39e…, and the three `moe-runtime-*/1` versions).
- A new describe block feeds the packaged manifest's own report into `createCompatGate` — the landed control-room authority, which this task deliberately does not reimplement — and requires `ok: true`. That is the actual proof: had the pins been stale literals, that gate would refuse.
- Two negative controls stop it being vacuous: a manifest built with `moe-runtime-command/9` and a manifest built with a zeroed schema hash are each refused by that same gate. The pin case additionally asserts `truthClass: "OBSERVED"`, which is the control room's own marker, so the refusal is attributable to that layer rather than to my distribution gate.

BRIDGE/LOADABILITY: both tooling modules are imported in a real `node --experimental-strip-types` child process from the repo root, asserting DEFINED bindings rather than exit 0 — a process that imports nothing also exits 0, and an import cycle yields a TDZ-undefined binding that imports cleanly and dies at first use. This is the leg vitest cannot provide, since it resolves NodeNext `.js` back to `.ts`.

Green on the first run again. Still not treating that as evidence — step 7's mutation drill decides whether these assertions are load-bearing.

implementationPlan.description: Adversarial review and mutation drill, after implementation and before the final gate. Review concurrency/repeated invocation, empty/null/huge/hostile records, duplicate IDs and normalized/case-fold path collisions, untrusted or throwing crypto ports, truncated containers, swapped signatures, all-stale-but-mutually-consistent sets, changed asset bytes, missing/extra components, and external skill same-ID substitution. Confirm no result grants command/effect/lifecycle authority. Mutate the production source-SHA comparison so a validly signed stale manifest is admitted and prove the targeted test goes red with its exact reason/layer assertion; mutate the artifact-case list and prove the exact case-count/set assertion goes red; corrupt the production signature path and prove the signature test—not syntax failure—goes red. Restore each file by captured checksum, confirm no probe/generated-evidence files remain, and verify every production source is <=250 lines (mandatory split before 400).
implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial review found a REAL DEFECT, which is fixed and now drilled. 9 mutation drills run, 8 killed their target, 1 survived and I report it below with why it proves nothing.

DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED — the packager could emit a container that can never be admitted.
`distribution-build.ts` accumulated the asset payload by assigning into an object literal: `payload[path] = base64`. For the path `__proto__` that assignment creates NO own property and is silently discarded (measured: `Object.hasOwn` false, `Object.keys` empty, prototype unchanged — assigning a string to the `__proto__` accessor is a no-op). The manifest would still DECLARE that asset, so the build returned `ok` while producing a container whose asset key set can never equal the declared set. Startup would refuse it with ASSET_SET_MISMATCH — fail-closed, so not a security hole, but a packager that reports success for an unusable artifact is a defect.
Fix: collect `[path, base64]` pairs and materialise with `Object.fromEntries`, which uses CreateDataProperty and therefore creates a real own `__proto__` key (measured: own key true, prototype intact, JSON round-trips). Duplicate detection moved from `Object.hasOwn(payload, path)` to an explicit `Set`, since the old check inherited the same blind spot. Drilled: D7 restores the naive `reduce`-into-a-literal form and the new test goes red.
Worth noting the asymmetry that hid this: `JSON.parse('{"__proto__":"x"}')` DOES create an own data property, so the READ path was always correct and only the WRITE path was broken. A round-trip test built from parsed JSON would never have caught it.

THREE TESTS ADDED from the review, each covering a listed adversarial case that had no assertion:
- A signature lifted from a different component must not admit this one (the "swapped signatures" case).
- An asset path shadowing Object.prototype packages and admits (the defect above).
- Admission grants identifiers only: the startup result's key set is exactly `["launched","ok"]`, every launched value is a string, no value is a function, and the result is frozen. Together with the contract suite's equivalent on `verifyDistributionSet`, this is the "no result grants command/effect/lifecycle authority" check.

MUTATION DRILLS. Every drill neutralised an OPERAND with a constant; no line was ever deleted, since a deleted line out of a multi-line condition is a syntax error that reddens the suite for the wrong reason. Each drill captured the file's sha256 before, restored from the captured text in a `finally`, and re-hashed after — restore was verified against the checksum, NOT against `git status`, because these files were swept into a foreign commit mid-task and `git status` is not a reliable witness here. Failed SUITES were counted as well as failed tests, output was scanned for `SyntaxError|Transform failed|Cannot find module`, and each drill asserted the NAMES of the tests that had to go red.

| Drill | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | source-SHA comparison -> `false` | 2 suites / 3 tests red, incl. the stale-but-consistent case |
| D2 | artifact case list ID renamed | 1 suite / 2 tests red, the exact-ID assertion |
| D3a | packager signs a constant instead of the manifest bytes | 1 suite / 10 tests red |
| D3b | signature verification `|| true` | 1 suite / 3 tests red, incl. the swapped-signature case |
| D4 | duplicate-component guard -> `false` | 2 suites / 2 tests red |
| D5 | trusted-key check -> `false` | 1 suite / 2 tests red, incl. the port-never-called spy |
| D6 | backslash path rule -> `false` | 1 suite / 1 test red |
| D7 | `Object.fromEntries` -> reduce into a literal | 1 suite / 1 test red |
| D8 | componentId blanked out of the signed bytes | **SURVIVED** |

D8 SURVIVED, and the honest reading is that the mutation was badly chosen rather than that a test is missing. Blanking componentId from `canonicalUnsignedManifestBytes` changes both the signing and the verifying side identically, so it does not isolate componentId coverage — and the two containers in that test differ in assets, aggregateDigest and componentKind as well, so the lifted signature still fails for those reasons. The property "a lifted signature is refused" is nonetheless proven load-bearing by D3b, which reddens exactly that test. I am not claiming a componentId-specific drill; I am reporting that the one I designed was uninformative.

REVIEW OF THE REMAINING LISTED CASES: concurrency and repeated invocation are safe by construction — a grep for module-level `let`/`var` or mutable `[]`/`{}`/`Map`/`Set` bindings across all five production modules returns nothing, so every function is pure over its arguments with no shared state to race. Empty/null/huge/hostile records, duplicate IDs, case-fold path collisions, untrusted and throwing crypto ports, truncated containers, all-stale-but-consistent sets, changed asset bytes, missing/extra/duplicate components and same-ID skill substitution all have named assertions in the two suites.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Chosen: a packaging-time signed container plus a production startup admission gate. This keeps daemon, control-room, MCP, provider, and future IDE sources thin: packaging embeds the manifest and the generated artifact can launch only through one verifier. It also stays inside the owned distribution/tooling paths instead of editing five unrelated consumers.
Rejected: adding independent compatibility checks to daemon, UI, MCP, and provider modules. That would fork the existing authority: createCompatGate already owns the control-room contract-pin decision and apps/daemon/src/http/http-adapter.ts already maps wire drift to DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH.
Rejected: treating the absent JetBrains adapter as if it were built. adapters/jetbrains is absent and task-9fd52b41f3ea4aad8c0c07bbe6fd3025 explicitly depends on this task. This task must publish and exercise the IDE_ADAPTER packaging/startup contract, while task-9fd52b41f3ea4aad8c0c07bbe6fd3025 is the named real consumer; tests must not claim a real JetBrains binary exists.
Rejected: deriving a second schema authority or embedding signing secrets. Build input must use the existing generated contract digest/pins, and callers inject an Ed25519 signing key plus trusted public-key map. Release publication, key provisioning, and secret persistence remain out of scope.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Verified on disk at planning time: packages/contracts/src/distribution, tools/packaging, tests/integration, adapters/jetbrains, and the root test:integration script are absent.
Existing compatibility surfaces are partial but authoritative for their seams. createCompatGate validates exact contractSchemaHash/apiCompatibilityRange and shape-checks buildToolVersions/sourceSha/assetDigest; daemon handleCommandRequest refuses protocolVersion drift at stage COMPATIBILITY with DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH. The new gate composes with these pins; it must not replace or restate lifecycle/authority semantics.
Built source components currently available for the integration inventory are daemon (apps/daemon/src/index.ts), control-room (apps/control-room/index.html plus its source assets), MCP (packages/mcp/src/index.ts), and the Claude/Codex provider adapter entrypoints. The integration sweep must assert this hand-reviewed inventory and its exact non-zero case count. IDE_ADAPTER is exercised as a packaging contract fixture only and its real consumer is task-9fd52b41f3ea4aad8c0c07bbe6fd3025.
The roadmap comment adds built-in skill bundles and durable instruction templates to every manifest. Reuse packages/skills/src/index.js -> validateSkillManifestBytes for skill identities instead of reimplementing skill validation. AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and .codex/agent-instructions.md are the current durable instruction sources; pin their exact IDs/count/digests in the integration inventory. Runtime/user/project skills remain separate provenance inputs and never enter or override built-in entries.
Raw Node does not resolve a .js specifier to a .ts file. New contracts modules therefore need one-line LF .js bridges because the packaging tools run under Node 24 --experimental-strip-types. Vitest alone is not sufficient proof of loadability.
planningNotes.risks:
Trust must not be self-derived. Startup expectations include the trusted source SHA/object format, schema hash, compatibility pins, exact component IDs, and key IDs; agreement among an entirely stale set is not admission. Missing expectation/key/signature/asset evidence returns DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH and no launch.
Ed25519 signing must cover canonical unsigned manifest bytes. Exclude wall time, temp directories, filesystem enumeration order, absolute paths, locale, and host separators; normalize logical paths to NFC forward-slash relative paths, reject traversal/drive/UNC/case-fold collisions, sort deterministically, and emit LF canonical bytes. This is required for Windows/macOS/Linux byte equality.
Every refusal test must assert code DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH, the stable reason, and refusedBy DISTRIBUTION_STARTUP (or DISTRIBUTION_PACKAGER for build-input refusals). A control-room/daemon refusal test must also pin that its existing compatibility layer refused. Never assert only ok:false or that launch was not called.
The generated inventory must not pass vacuously: assert the exact component case count, exact component IDs/kinds, exact durable-template count, and the explicit built-in-skill count, even when the current built-in-skill count is zero. A future shipped asset must make the hand-reviewed inventory check red until deliberately registered.
Keep each production TypeScript source at or below 250 physical lines and split before 400. The two contract modules and two tooling modules are intentionally separated by responsibility; one-line bridges are runtime support, not duplicate logic.
package.json is touched only for the task-mandated test:integration entry. Preserve foreign shared-tree work, never stage broadly, and use only explicit owned pathspecs.
